135:T11a7,## What & why

Closes #10769 (the named-entity half of #7007 / #10469).

The merged secret-swap layer masks **structured secrets** behind opaque
`__ELIZA_SECRET_…__` placeholders restored only at execution. That is the wrong
shape for **named-entity PII** — a contact's name, employer, city, street address —
which the model must reason over *coherently* but must never see for real.

This adds an **opt-in** (`ELIZA_PII_SWAP_ENABLED`, default off → zero behavior
change) pseudonymization layer around every `useModel` call: it detects named
entities with a small **local NER model** and swaps each for a *realistic*,
cached, reversible surrogate ("Dana Whitfield" → "Marco Hoffman", "Acme" →
"Ridgeline Holdings") before the provider call, then restores the real values at
the execution/reply boundary. The provider, trajectory, and logs see a fluent
prompt with **zero** real PII; the tool call and the user get the real values.

## How it works

- **`PseudonymSession`** (`packages/core/src/security/pii-pseudonymizer.ts`) — a
  per-turn, per-session-salted, bijective, collision-checked surrogate vault.
  Substitution is a **single-pass, boundary-aware** regex over `values ∪
  surrogates` (longest-first): idempotent (the runtime substitutes twice per call),
  never corrupts benign substrings ("John" ≠ "Johnson"), and the exact inverse on
  restore. The only hard rule on a surrogate is `surrogate != original`.
- **Recognizer seam** (`entity-recognizer.ts`) — an async `PiiEntityRecognizer`
  interface, a dependency-free `RegexEntityRecognizer` (street addresses; opt-in
  email/phone), a `GazetteerEntityRecognizer`, and a `CompositeEntityRecognizer`
  (overlap resolution + blocklist + distilbert-label canonicalization). Swaps by
  **value**, so it's robust to transformers.js null offsets (#359).
- **Runtime wiring** — behind `ELIZA_PII_SWAP_ENABLED`, `useModel` runs one awaited
  `learn()` then substitutes (after the secret pass, so the NER model reads secret
  *placeholders*, never raw keys); `execute-planned-tool-call` restores real
  names/orgs/addresses into handler args (incl. the REPLY text). Turn-scoped via
  `trajectory-context`, mirroring the secret session.
- **`@elizaos/plugin-pii-guard`** — supplies the local **`dslim/distilbert-NER`**
  model (Apache-2.0, person/org/location) via `@huggingface/transformers` v3 /
  onnxruntime-node, injected through `PII_ENTITY_RECOGNIZER_SERVICE`. Core never
  hard-depends on an ONNX runtime; without the plugin the layer runs regex-only.
  (transformers.js v3 returns raw per-token BIO with null offsets for BERT, so the
  plugin stitches BIO + re-locates each entity's exact substring itself.)

Composes with the secret-swap layer; the model saw only surrogates so it can only
emit surrogates. Model choice: distilbert-NER is Apache-2.0 with a first-party ONNX
export and is the only small model natively covering **Organization**; Piiranha is
`cc-by-nc-nd` (non-commercial → rejected).

## Evidence

- **Live model** (`.github/issue-evidence/10469-pii-ner/`): a Cerebras
  `gpt-oss-120b` trajectory — the provider received *"Marco Hoffman at Ridgeline
  Holdings / 5591 Cypress Court"*, the real *Dana Whitfield / Acme Robotics / 1600
  Amphitheatre Parkway* never left the process, and `SEND_EMAIL` ran with the real
  recipient. The real distilbert-NER model was run live too (person 0.94 / org 0.94
  / location 0.97).
- **Offline tests (PR CI): 58**
  - 3000-iteration seeded fuzz: round-trip, no-leak (surrogate-masked), bijection,
    idempotency, determinism, boundary-safety — caught 2 real bugs before commit.
  - unit (pseudonymizer, recognizers), ingress + egress runtime tests, plugin
    relocate/recognizer tests.
- Core `typecheck` clean; biome clean.
- **Adversarial review pass** (4 lenses — leak-paths / round-trip / wiring /
  arch — each finding independently skeptic-verified against the real code)
  found and this PR fixes: a HIGH cross-call surrogate/value collision that could
  misdeliver a restored tool arg (now covered by a 1500-iteration multi-call
  fuzz), an IMAGE-prompt swap bypass, a pre_model-hook fresh-PII gap, a
  TEXT_EMBEDDING retrieval regression, and a throwing-recognizer crash path.

## Test plan

`bun run --cwd packages/core test` (security + runtime PII suites) ·
`bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-pii-guard test` · live lanes gated on
`CEREBRAS_API_KEY` / model download (excluded from PR CI).

136:T5d4,The iOS device build (`ELIZA_IOS_FULL_BUN_ENGINE=1`) fails to compile:

```
KeepAwakeBridge.swift:34:13: error: value of type 'JSContext' has no member 'installBridgeFunction'
** BUILD FAILED **  (xcodebuild exited with code 65)
```

#11897 split the JSContext `keep_awake_set` installer into `KeepAwakeBridge+JSContext.swift` specifically so the core `KeepAwakeBridge` type stays **JavaScriptCore-free** and compiles into the full-Bun engine build — whose podspec (`ElizaosCapacitorBunRuntime.podspec`, `include_full_bun_engine` branch) omits `JavaScriptCore` and lists only a minimal source set (no `JSContextHelpers.swift`, no `+JSContext.swift`). But the base `KeepAwakeBridge.swift` still carried a leftover `install(into ctx: JSContext)` (+ `import JavaScriptCore`) that calls `ctx.installBridgeFunction` — the extension defined in the excluded `JSContextHelpers.swift`. So the full-Bun build can't resolve it (and the compat build would hit a redeclaration vs the `+JSContext` extension).

Removed the duplicate installer + import from the core file. The JSContext install now lives solely in `KeepAwakeBridge+JSContext.swift` (compat build); the full-Bun path drives the same ref-counted holder via `setEnabled` from `FullBunEngineHost`.

Verified by re-running `ios:device:deploy` to a physical iPhone (build proceeds past the Swift compile). Native/on-device evidence attached once the device install completes.

## What landed

**Real 3D renderer — `XRSpatialScene`** (`packages/ui/src/spatial/xr-scene.tsx` +
`xr-scene-math.ts`). Authored views are placed as panels at world poses
(position, orientation, depth), billboarded to face a movable headset camera, and
projected to screen by a deterministic pinhole camera. A controller's **world**
ray is intersected with the panel planes; the nearest hit maps back to a DOM
element (`data-agent-id` preserved), so "the right controller hit `save`" is a
computed 3D fact, not a pixel guess. A `move` `SpatialAction` relocates a panel in
world space. The math core is pure + unit-tested.

**Harness extended to 3D** (`plugins/plugin-xr/simulator`). The IWER emulator gains
a 3D-scene mode: world-space hit-tests, panel world positions, head/controller
pose read-back, real press (clicks the resolved DOM element so the **authored
handler** fires) and grab-drag. `scene.spec.ts` drives the loop over the gallery
views and captures screenshot + per-frame pose/hit JSON.

**Dedupe (#9941).** The byte-identical XR harness is collapsed: `plugin-facewear/
emulator` now re-exports the single canonical `@elizaos/plugin-xr` simulator.

**Dead/mock e2e fixed (#9968).** `camera-pose.spec.ts` is un-skipped and driven by
the real `window.__XREmulator`; `all-views-crud` + `voice-forms` hit the **real**
`view-host` route via `route-server.ts`; the `view-server.mjs` mock is **deleted**.

**Parity gate for XR (#9946).** The `registered-view-parity` xr branch now mounts
the real `XRSpatialScene` and asserts 3D placement (depth > 0, in front of head) +
scene infra for **every** registered view — not a duplicate flat DOM mount.

states the real status. The `xr-harness-e2e` job builds the scene bundle and runs
both the 3D scene loop and the facewear real-route e2e.
